subject: CFA warning not identified but df > 0

messages.author: 0f8a40c4f8f833a4
messages.subject: CFA warning not identified but df > 0
parts:
Hii, 

When I try to fit the (orhtogonal) model below I get two warnings: 

cfa_4comp_var <- '
comp1 =~ consc1 + consc2 + consc3 + consc4 + imagin2 + imagin3
comp2 =~ benevol1 + benevol2 + benvol3 + benov4
comp3 =~ extraver1 + extraver2 + extraver3 + extraver4 + benvol5 + imagin1
comp4 =~ emo_stab1 + emo_stab2
'
cfa_4comp_var_fit <- cfa(cfa_4comp_var, data = hipic_full, orthogonal = T, estimator = "ML")

Warning messages: 
1: In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats, : lavaan WARNING: Could not compute standard errors! The information matrix could not be inverted. This may be a symptom that the model is not identified. 
2: In lav_object_post_check(object) : lavaan WARNING: some estimated ov variances are negative

Given degrees of freedom >  0 , I do not understand why this model is not identified. 
I calculated degrees of freedom as follows: 
df = number of unique covariances - number of free parameters =  ((0.5*18 *19) - (14 loadings +18 variable variances + 4 factor variances) = 135

messages.author: 9b7a59c6f2d552cc
messages.subject: Re: CFA warning not identified but df > 0
parts:
it has nothing to do wtih df.
the warning is that you have negative error variances somewhere in the data. these can be fixed to a small positive number or the item removed.
you need to check what the residual values are.

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: CFA warning not identified but df > 0
parts:
Vibeke,

Negative correlations and covariances are not a concern, just variances. For a trivial example, income and homelessness would be negatively correlated.

The identification problem for the first message was, as you're starting to see, that you had only two indicators for comp4. In a CFA, each factor needs at least three indicators in the absence of additional constraints to be identified.

Non-negative degrees of freedom is necessary for identification of the full model, but not sufficient, because parts of a model can be locally unidentified, as was your case with comp4.

Pat
